authentication.provisioning: DFMCP_BRIDGE_TOKEN environment variable inherited by Dwarf Fortress/DFHack
authentication.limitations: Protects against accidental and unauthenticated loopback callers; it is not a defense against a process that can read the DFHack process environment or memory.

canonicalization.strings: UTF-8 protobuf strings truncated only at valid code point boundaries
canonicalization.reply_complete: true only when every citizen in the requested canonical range is returned

security_invariants: The V1 plugin registers no mutation RPC methods.
The V1 plugin does not register RunCommand, RunLua, keyboard, pause, dig, teleport, or arbitrary command forwarding.
Every plugin method authenticates before inspecting world state.
The plugin requests no SF_ALLOW_REMOTE flag and is intended only for the loopback DFHack remote server.
All repeated output is bounded by request and hard server ceilings.
Unit output is sorted by stable unit ID before pagination.
A partial page cannot prove absence outside its declared range.
The Rust process treats the plugin response as untrusted until bounds, nonce, versions, enum values, and canonical ordering validate.
No transport acknowledgment is a canonical observation until an ObservationCapsule validates and publishes.
acceptance: Plugin builds through DFHack's dfhack_plugin(... PROTOBUFS ...) macro.
Handshake rejects missing, short, wrong, or oversized tokens.
Handshake returns exact DF, DFHack, bridge, plugin protocol, world-loaded, and fortress-mode manifests.
ReadObservation is deterministic across two calls while the game is paused and unchanged.
Citizen pages concatenate to the same canonical roster as one sufficiently large page.
Rust decoder rejects noncanonical order, nonce mismatch, version mismatch, oversize strings, oversize pages, and trailing protobuf garbage.
One live reply produces one immutable canonical ObservationCapsule and an agent briefing with explicit complete/partial coverage.
No live mutation symbol or RPC is linked into the V1 plugin.
